decisions.slice: I-4-4D7: migrate the single open-pr reference evaluator validate_pr_body.py byte-for-byte (no legacy adaptation was necessary) and verify its two pure CLI entry points (--evaluate-reference-policy, --evaluate-native-auto-close-risk) through the real Python CLI with temporary body / facts files. No wrapper, new schema or permanent gate is added; the existing runner scripts/ci/run_stage1b1_tests.py is reused.
decisions.scope_limit: Only the pure evaluator moved. open-pr SKILL.md, open_pr.py / update_pr.py, the PR template, the normal PR body lint entry (it depends on unmigrated artifacts) and the full source test_validate_pr_body.py stay unmigrated and are not claimed as working or as run.
decisions.no_github_io: The evaluator performs no GitHub I/O; the closure feeds it fixtures only. It cannot close an Issue, change a closing relation or merge anything.
decisions.time_bound: A clear native result is time-bound: a human can change the final squash message or the closing relation afterwards, so the merge-time caller must re-run the check (fresh recheck) or merge the verified message unchanged (adopted_message_sha256). That recheck is a later runtime owner and was not run live here.

exit_code_contract.rule: The source CLI exits 0 for EVERY structured result, including fail_closed, body_verdict block / repair and native blocked / fail_closed. The exit code is a JSON transport status, not an allow decision. Only an unreadable --body-file exits 2 with empty stdout. Consumers must read the JSON.
exit_code_contract.negative_control: naive_exit_code_consumer accepts every blocked / fail_closed / repair result; strict consumers accept only body_verdict valid under a non-fail_closed decision and native status clear.
